items.title: Rs 48 lakh to 2 ex-judges, ‘doubtful voters’: A press club’s costly wait for an election
items.summary: In July 2024, a district court in Jammu handed two retired judges a clear job: get the Jammu Press Club to hold its overdue election, “by all means”, by September 30. It’s been over two years since, and the elections are nowhere in sight. The two former judges are still in place. And the club is still paying them Rs 1 lakh each a month to oversee its accounts: signing off on 49 member staff salaries, bar bills and daily supplies, either from the committee room, or the accounts office, or from their own homes when a club employee is sent over with paperwork. This seems to be a strange arrangement for a body of nearly 870 journalists: an institution whose members spend their working lives asking public offices why their processes have stalled, unable to run a ballot of its own for two years. The former judges refused to clearly specify the amount they have received so far, but by Newslaundry ’s estimates, the club has committed close to Rs 48 lakh to the two men since July 2024. This amount, some members say, could have gone towards repairs the building has not seen since years. Apart from the district court, the matter has also reached the high court. items.title: Filling the empty vessel: How the Supreme Court now attributes mens rea to companies
items.summary: Corporate criminal liability has always sat awkwardly with the basic idea of a guilty mind. A company, in the old line, has "no soul to damn and no body to kick." It can't form intent the way a person does. Still, companies hold enormous economic power and can-do real harm, so legal systems have had to find ways to make them answer for crimes. In India, the Supreme Court settled in Iridium India Telecom Ltd. v. Motorola Inc. , (2011) 1 SCC 74 , that a company can have mens rea . What it never explained was how : through whom, and on what basis. As the Court put it in Sanofi , that question remained "an empty vessel, yet to be filled." On September 7, 2026, the Court finally filled it with a three-stage framework, built after a careful look at English law from Lennard's Carrying through to the reforms that followed Barclays . This is the first time the Supreme Court has set out a complete doctrinal basis for attributing mens rea to a company. It will change how corporate prosecutions are brought, defended and decided. items.title: Extreme heat is putting pregnant women and newborns at greater risk, global survey finds
items.summary: Extreme heat is already affecting the health of pregnant women and newborns, with nearly three-quarters of maternal healthcare professionals surveyed across five countries reporting an increase in heat-related cases and complications over the past five years, a new survey commissioned by Wellcome has found. Wellcome is a global charitable foundation that supports science and research to address urgent health challenges, including climate change, infectious diseases and mental health A survey conducted last month of 1,000 healthcare professionals in India, Australia, Brazil, the UK and Zimbabwe found that 73% reported an increase in heat-related cases or complications affecting pregnant women, while 76% reported an increase affecting foetal or newborn health. Nearly all respondents said they had personally cared for a pregnant woman (98%) or a baby (99%) whose health they believed had been adversely affected by extreme heat. The findings were released ahead of the UN climate talks and come as extreme heat intensifies globally. items.title: ECI’s reforms cannot erase past failures
items.summary: Imagine you're a patient in a hospital and the hospital tells you: “From tomorrow, we’ll maintain proper records of every important decision about your treatment. We’ll make sure doctors can make the decisions without being overridden by a computer system. And if something goes wrong, we’ll investigate what happened.” You are not going to say, “Waah - Great reforms.” You would ask: “Hello, Wait. What was happening till yesterday?” That is exactly where we need to begin with the Election Commission of India. After months of questions over its functioning, the ECI has suddenly announced a series of changes: agendas will be circulated, minutes recorded, IT systems screened, and some SIR-affected voters given additional assistance. But these aren't just changes for tomorrow. They raise questions about what happened yesterday: what procedures were followed, who made the decisions, and who authorised them? Let Me Explain. items.title: Rs 9 crore for Sanjay Dutt-starrer on RSS: The state broadcaster’s favourite box-office flop
items.summary: There is a neat trick some films manage that ordinary films can't: lose money in cinemas and still come out ahead in a government ledger. Aakhri Sawal , starring Sanjay Dutt, has pulled it off. Released on May 15, 2026, after a promotional campaign built around the RSS’s role in some of modern India’s most contested episodes, the film reportedly earned Rs 2.45 crore in its theatrical run – a number Bollywood Hungama ’s box-office data files under “ flop ”. It reportedly cost around Rs 30 crore to make. By conventional arithmetic, that’s a loss hard to recover from. Except Prasar Bharati doesn’t appear to have read it that way. Copies of documents from the public broadcaster’s Content Sourcing Division, reviewed by Newslaundry , show it had spent Rs 4.28 crore on the film by June 2026, with another Rs 4.65 crore projected by March 2027 – a total outlay of Rs 8.93 crore. Prasar Bharati’s name appears in the film’s credit roll as a co-producer. What did the money buy? Was it a stake in the film and its royalties or just a licence to stream it? items.title: How India’s food prices rose this September
items.summary: In September 2026, a kilogram of onion cost 93% more than last year, while sugar prices were up 28% and rice was up about 8%, on average, according to ISignal’s Food Price Watch dashboard , which uses Department of Consumer Affairs data. This is in a year with the fourth lowest rainfall since the turn of the century, as the country approaches the withdrawal of the monsoon with a 13% deficit. Sustained low prices in past years pushed farmers away from onion, experts say, while the government lists factors such as increased demand and speculation for the increase in sugar prices. “Extreme climate events are raising agricultural risk, disrupting the global food system, increasing the chance of multiple breadbasket failure and pushing up food prices around the world,” a September 2026 analysis by Zero Carbon Analytics noted, adding that “historically unprecedented heat, drought, rain and cold are causing food price spikes across all continents”. It also noted that perishable foods such as fruits and vegetables can face larger price swings because of their limited shelf life and more vulnerable supply chains.
